newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's CPC says no longer seeking Syncrude stake.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's CPC says no longer seeking Syncrude stake.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Friday it was no longer seeking to buy a stake in Syncrude Canada Ltd, which controls a major oil field in Alberta, Canada.
"After repeatedly failing in attempts in purchase shares from Syncrude's major holders, Chinese Petroleum has decided to give up the plan," company spokeswoman Ho Li-chun said.
Chinese Petroleum had hoped to import Syncrude's oil after becoming a partial owner, she said.
Chinese Petroleum had budgeted $110 million for a plan to acquire five percent of Syncrude Canada's shares in 1995, but those shares were purchased by Torch Energy Royalty Trust.

Taiwan's oil giant subsequently sought to purchase holdings of other shareholders, but was unable to do so, the spokeswoman said. Chinese Petroleum had notified the Ministry of Economics of its decision, she added.
Syncrude controls an oil field in Alberta with proven reserves of over 20 million barrels of low sulfur crude, Ho said. -- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
